title: Numbers
cando: count to 20, and say your age, a phone number and a price

about.text: In this lesson you count to twenty. You say your age and phone number. You ask: How much is it?
goals: Say your age: I am thirty.
Say a phone number, figure by figure.
Ask: How many? How much is it?

chapters.title: How many?
chapters.text:
Numbers are everywhere.
Carlos joins a sports centre.
The receptionist asks: How old are you?
She asks for his phone number.
Carlos asks: How much is it?
Listen for fifteen and fifty.

chapters.title: Numbers and phone numbers
chapters.text:
Count with me: one, two, three … twenty.
Eleven and twelve are new words.
Thirteen to nineteen end in teen.
Thirty-four is thirty and four.
Say phone numbers figure by figure.
Stop after three or four figures.

chapters.title: A price list
chapters.text:
Next, you read a price list.
Read the prices slowly.
Then you write 0 to 20.
And you write numbers about you.

chapters.title: Numbers at the café
chapters.text:
Then you swap numbers with a friend.
Write the number down.
Say it back to check it.
Ask two prices. How much is the tea?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story.
It has numbers in it.
Read it two times. Find the numbers.

warmup.prompt: Where do you use numbers every day?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. We use numbers in all three places.

conversation.title: How many?
conversation.setting: Carlos joins a sports centre. He talks to the receptionist.

questions.why: The receptionist says: Fifteen. One, five.
The receptionist says: Three classes a week.

phrases.use: Asking about a number of things.
Saying a number figure by figure.

items.meaning: Say numbers in order: one, two, three.
A question about a number of things.
items.example: How many people are here today?

items.meaning: Not young. We also use it for age.
How many years old you are.
items.example: Write your age on the form.

items.meaning: You use it to call a person.

items.example: My phone number starts with zero.

sound.title: thirteen or thirty
sound.explain: These numbers sound close. In thirteen, the end is strong: thir-TEEN. In thirty, the start is strong: THIR-ty. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Carlos's lines. Record yourself. Then listen. Are your numbers clear?

spot.instructions: Look at these lines from the conversation. Each one has a number.
spot.question: How does Carlos say his phone number? One big number, or figure by figure?
spot.answer: Figure by figure: zero, seven, seven, zero, zero. He stops after a small group. How many classes? The answer is a number: three.

rules.title: Numbers and phone numbers
rule: How many + things? How many classes? Three.
Phone numbers: figure by figure, in small groups.
0 is zero or oh. 4 4 is double four.
rules.mistake: Not: How many class? Say: How many classes?

practice.q: How ___ are you? I am thirty.
You see 0 7 7 in a phone number. You say: ___
practice.why: Say phone numbers figure by figure.

practice.q: How many days in a week?

yourTurn.prompt: Say three numbers about you. Your age, your phone number, your house number. They can be made up.
yourTurn.model: I am thirty-four years old. My phone number is 0 7 7 0 0, 9 0 0, 5 2 8. My house number is 12.

gist.why: It says: Pay by cash or card.

items.meaning: How much you pay for something.
items.example: What's the price of the milk?

items.meaning: You pay with it: coins and notes.
items.example: My money is in my bag.

write.task: Copy the figures 0 to 20. Then write four numbers about you. Copy the model. Change the numbers.
checklist: My phone number is in small groups.
Every number is a figure: 12, not twelve.

card.title: Numbers at the café
card.situation: You are at a café with Ana. Ana is new at your work. You want her phone number. You want a tea and a cake.
card.goal: Give your number. Write down Ana's number. Ask two prices.

prepare.notes: Write your phone number in small groups. Say it slowly. You can use a made-up number.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, find a partner. Say your phone number. Use a made-up number. Write down your partner's number. Then ask the teacher two prices.
doIt.wehel: You are my new friend from work. We are in a café. Ask for my phone number. Then say your number slowly. Then you work in the café. I ask two prices. Use very simple English.

model.title: At the café
lines: Excuse me. How much is the tea?
A tea and a cake, please.
compare: I say my number in small groups.
I write down the other number.
I check it: I say it back.

canDo: I can count from zero to twenty.
I can say my phone number.
I can write down a phone number.
I can ask: How much is it?

reading.before: Look at the pictures. Can you see numbers? Say them.
reading.talk: Find three numbers in the story. Say them to Wehel, or write them.

quiz.q: How ___ are you? I am forty.
It's one, five. Is it fifteen or fifty?
In a phone number, 0 is zero or ___ .
I am 30 years old. 30 is my ___ .
quiz.why: Your age is how old you are.
What is your name? asks for a name.
Say please when you ask for something.

liveClass: Day 1: count round the class to 20, then back to zero. Then the sports centre conversation in pairs. Change the age and the price.
Day 2: the task. Learners swap made-up phone numbers and write them down. Then they ask you two prices.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then a listening game: say 13 or 30, 14 or 40. Learners write the figure.
